html:
The Tsáchila are an Indigenous people of the western lowland forest of Ecuador, in the province of Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas, which is partly named after them. Spanish speakers called them Colorados, "the coloured ones", because the men dye their hair red with achiote paste, cut in a helmet shape.

Their language, Tsafiki, belongs to the Barbacoan family, like that of their northern neighbours the Chachi; its name means "true word". Their healers, the pone, are known across Ecuador, and many outsiders visit them. Highland peoples such as the Otavalo lived to their east.
